title: Development of an automated machine learning-based prognostic prediction model for emergency septic shock patients.
summary: In a retrospective single-center cohort of 913 emergency septic-shock patients, an Improved Red Fox Optimization algorithm tuned an AutoML model for 28-day mortality. On the held-out 183-patient test set, the model had ROC-AUC 0.891 and PR-AUC 0.879 and outperformed SOFA, APACHE II and qSOFA in the reported comparison. This internal evaluation does not establish prospective clinical benefit.
ai_technology: A learned model predicted 28-day mortality in a defined emergency septic-shock patient cohort and was compared with clinical scores.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The primary abstract reports 913 patients from one tertiary hospital, split into 730 training and 183 test records; an IRFO-optimized AutoML model achieved test ROC-AUC 0.8911 and PR-AUC 0.8790. The source also reports comparison with SOFA, APACHE II and qSOFA, plus decision-curve analysis. The evidence is retrospective and single-center, without external or prospective workflow validation.
evidence.unknown: This retrospective single-center holdout does not establish external generalization or prospective clinical benefit; decision-curve analysis is not an observed improvement in patient outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: A learned model predicted 28-day mortality in a defined emergency septic-shock patient cohort and was compared with clinical scores.
